newsitem.title: INDIA: Good overseas demand boosts India soymeal prices.
newsitem.headline: Good overseas demand boosts India soymeal prices.

text.p: Indian soymeal export prices rose by nearly $20 per tonne in the last week due to a surge in overseas demand, traders said on Tuesday.
Soymeal export prices were currently $275 per tonne FAS, up from last week's $255, but exporters are waiting for prices to firm further before signing new contracts, traders said.
"Selling from Indian (soymeal) exporters is limited because they are waiting for better prices," said Sunil Saboo, a leading oilmeal broker.
Traders said Indian exporters have signed contracts to export nearly 700,000 tonnes of soymeal for November, December and January shipments.
Switzerland-based company Miner Mat recently contracted to buy Indian soymeal. Details of the contracts were not available, traders said.
They said main buyers were China, Indonesia and Far Eastern countries. Pakistan and Bangladesh had also signed deals to import Indian soymeal.
In local markets soybeans were quoted at 9,750-10,000 rupees per tonne and 10,100-10,250 rupees in plant delivery conditions, traders said.
Around 10,000 tonnes of soybeans per day were arriving in the markets of central India, the hub of India's soybean processing industry. --Mohan Narvaria New Delhi newsroom +91-11 301 2024
